source.title: Mechanistic Permutability: Match Features Across Layers
source.authors: Nikita Balagansky; Ian Maksimov; Daniil Gavrilov

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how well SAE features can be matched across layers in language models, using parameter similarity, feature-description judgments, and hidden-state approximation. This bears on whether SAE-derived features behave as stable, recoverable units, but it does not directly test superposition in toy networks.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern SAE feature matching, matching across layers, and layer-pruning approximations. Background statements about superposition and cited results are not study results. The study does not directly test feature overlap geometry, capacity pressure, or whether neurons are polysemantic.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It takes pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs and Neuronpedia descriptions as given and introduces SAE Match, a way to align features across layers. Every result reports how well that method performs: folded versus unfolded matching, GPT-4o-mini judgments of matched descriptions, explained variance and ∆L for layer pruning, and sensitivity to l0. The authors blame early-layer failures on SAE l0 mismatches, a property of their pipeline, not on whether the model's features exist. Superposition is stated as an assumption in the background. No result measures whether features are overlapping directions, whether capacity drives polysemanticity, whether SAE dictionaries are complete or canonical, or whether features are 1-D. Cross-layer persistence of matched features is a different construct from V5's stability and canonicity of a dictionary, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAE Match with parameter folding aligns SAE features across Gemma 2 layers without data. They find that some features persist over multiple layers and that matched features can approximate the next hidden state, especially after layer 10. Limitations they name: early-layer matching failures linked to l0 differences, sensitivity to l0, and features left unmatched by the bijective scheme. They also claim the method applies to LLaMA-3.1-8B (Figures 13 and 19).
record.recipe_differences: This study aligns pretrained SAE parameters across layers and evaluates matching and hidden-state approximation in language models; it does not reproduce the original toy-network feature-training or geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Matching quality varies with parameter folding, layer depth, distance between layers, SAE l0-norm, and the selected SAE set.

fits_no_version.finding: Features matched by SAE parameters keep similar LLM-judged descriptions for about five layers after layers 10, 12 and 20 in Gemma 2. Matching largely fails before layer 10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in residual-stream LLMs persist, permuted, across several adjacent layers in later layers.

record.problems: SAEs and feature descriptions are supplied by other work; feature similarity is judged by an external LLM rather than ground truth. Most plotted results are not numerically reported in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are stated. The authors note weak matching in early layers, dependence on SAE l0-norm, and that some features are not matched by the bijective scheme.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 11, 13, 16, and 17 report additional layer-approximation or quantile-matching plots, but the text provides no sufficiently specific outcome for a separate row bearing on the claim versions. Figure 13 also shows an application to LLAMA-3.1-8B, but the supplied text gives no textual result description for that figure.
record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. All rows measure the study's own method's matching or approximation quality, and superposition is assumed in the background. The reader's V4 and V5 labels are removed. V5 concerns completeness and canonicity of SAE dictionaries, which matching quality under a chosen SAE set cannot show. The authors attribute early-layer failures to their SAE choice, not to the model's representation.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment or test of overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent geometric transition, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test whether limited capacity causes neuron polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test other causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Uses pretrained SAEs and their feature descriptions; does not establish ground-truth completeness of their recovered features or measure how many neurons each feature spans.
Tests matching and persistence of SAE features across layers, not whether the dictionary is complete or whether its features are canonical in a broader sense.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared folded-parameter MSE after matching with folded parameters versus matching without folding.

conditions.value: consecutive SAE layers across the model

rows.measure: MSE of matched SAE parameters evaluated with folded parameters
rows.value: folded matching had lower MSE; unfolded matching consistently had higher MSE in the hidden-state scale
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the result; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (folded matching) with its unfolded variant. This is method performance, not a result on any version; it should not be a claim row.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared external-LLM judgments of feature-description matches for folded and unfolded matching.

conditions.value: tested layer pairs; evaluation shown by layer

rows.measure: External-LLM categories for matched feature descriptions: SAME, MAYBE, DIFFERENT
rows.value: folded matching exhibited improved feature-matching quality compared with the unfolded variant
rows.note: The authors caution that folding also makes the judgments more optimistic, including for deeper layers.
rows.check: Own-method comparison, folded versus unfolded, judged by GPT-4o-mini. The authors note folding makes labels more optimistic. Not a result on any version.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated matched features across layers using feature descriptions and paired feature activations.

conditions.value: initial layers, up to the 10th layer

rows.measure: External-LLM SAME judgments for matched features
rows.value: The number of SAME features remained near zero in the initial layers; the authors state that SAE Match fails to align similar features there.
rows.note: The finding is stated in the text; the figure provides the plotted results.
rows.check: Near-zero SAME matches in early layers is a matching failure; authors attribute it to l0 differences between SAEs. It says nothing about whether SAE features are the model's units.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated matched features across layers using feature descriptions.
rows.measure: External-LLM SAME judgments for matched features
rows.baseline: initial layers, where SAME judgments were near zero
rows.value: SAME features began to increase after the 10th layer
rows.note: The increase supports feature similarity in later layers, but the study does not claim that all features match.
rows.check: Matching quality after layer 10 measures the method's success. It is not evidence on V4 or V5.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Measured paired feature activation for matched features across layers.

conditions.value: folded, with comparison to other matching variants

rows.measure: Matching Score, the probability of paired feature activation between matched layers
rows.value: The score followed a pattern similar to the feature-description evaluation, but did not drop to zero in early layers
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative trend; the score values are plotted.
rows.check: Matching Score is a performance metric of SAE Match.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Matched features from starting layers to subsequent layers using full permutation matrices.
rows.measure: Average external-LLM feature-similarity score, with DIFFERENT=1, MAYBE=2, SAME=3
rows.value: Feature similarity gradually declined but remained significant for approximately five layers; the authors also report good matches when evaluating full permutation matrices
rows.note: Results are plotted separately by starting layer; no numeric scores are stated in the text.
rows.check: Persistence of matched feature descriptions across about five layers is a cross-layer construct, not V5's completeness or canonicity. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared composed permutations with directly evaluated permutations for matching features across layers.
rows.value: Composed permutations performed adequately for nearby SAEs, especially in later layers, then began to diverge as distance increased
rows.note: The text says this distance-related decline supports the paper's composition hypothesis.
rows.check: Composed versus exact permutations is an internal method comparison (Hypothesis 3).

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Pruned layers using an encode-permute-decode operation and measured language-model loss change.

conditions.value: pruning each layer; the text highlights results starting from the 10th layer

rows.value: The smallest performance drop was on OpenWebText; starting from the 10th layer, pruning resulted in minimal performance loss
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative account; no numeric loss values are stated.
rows.check: Layer-pruning ∆L evaluates the method as an approximation tool.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Pruned layers using an encode-permute-decode operation and measured language-model loss change.

conditions.value: pruning each layer, including the last layer

rows.value: A decrease in quality was noted at the last layer of the Code dataset
rows.note: The text does not state the numeric size of the decrease.
rows.check: Layer-pruning ∆L on the Code dataset is method performance.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Swept SAE mean l0-norm and measured hidden-state approximation using feature matching.

conditions.value: five SAEs with different mean l0-norms on the 20th and 21st layers

rows.measure: Explained variance of approximated hidden states
rows.value: Explained variance peaked when mean l0-norm was approximately 70
rows.note: The text attributes the peak to a balance: very sparse SAEs may not reconstruct adequately, while above 100 active features matching all features becomes more difficult and noisy features can impair the estimate.
rows.check: Explained-variance peak near l0≈70 is a hyperparameter sensitivity of the matching method.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Swept SAE mean l0-norm and measured language-model loss change for feature-matching approximations.

conditions.value: five SAEs with different mean l0-norms on the 20th and 21st layers

rows.value: Higher mean l0-norm corresponded to a lower loss difference across all methods
rows.note: The authors explain that higher l0-norm SAEs capture more information and tend to give better approximations.
rows.check: ∆L versus l0 is method and SAE-reconstruction sensitivity, not a test of any version.

rows.subject: Gemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared hidden-state approximation using SAEs with more similar l0-norms across layers.

conditions.value: Neuronpedia SAEs versus selected GemmaScope SAEs with more similar l0-norms

rows.value: Reducing l0-norm differences between layers led to a better explained-variance metric
rows.note: This result concerns matching and approximation quality under a change of SAE set, not a direct test of the underlying model's feature geometry.
rows.check: Choosing a different SAE set to improve matching is a method-configuration comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma 2 SAE features in later layers and the tested layer-pruning settings
reader_labels.reason: The study reports increasing feature-description matches after layer 10 and minimal loss from pruning starting at layer 10 on OpenWebText, consistent with useful SAE-recovered features in these settings (R4, R6, R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Initial layers and variation in SAE sparsity
reader_labels.reason: Feature-description matches were near zero in initial layers, and approximation quality depended on SAE l0-norm, peaking at approximately 70 (R3, R10, R11).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Later Gemma 2 layers and nearby layer matches
reader_labels.reason: Matched features showed similarity that remained significant for approximately five layers, and composed matches worked adequately for nearby SAEs (R6, R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Initial layers, more distant layer matches, and varying SAE sparsity
reader_labels.reason: Matching fails to align similar features in initial layers, composed matches diverge with distance, and explained variance depends on sparsity (R3, R7, R10, R12).
